Herodes Atticus with his wife, the Roman Aristocrat Aspasia Annia Regilla, had erected a great outdoor nymphaeum (a monumental fountain) at Olympia, Greece. [2] Herodes Atticus
Herodes Atticus (, "Hērōidēs ho Attikos"; 177), or Atticus Herodes, was a distinguished and rich Greek aristocrat and sophist who served as a Roman senator. Appointed consul at Rome in 143, he was the first Greek to hold the rank of "consul ordinarius", as opposed to "consul suffectus". In Latin, his full name was given as Lucius Vibullius Hipparchus Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes (). According to Philostratus, Herodes Atticus was a notable proponent of the Second Sophistic. M.I. Finley described Herodes Atticus as "patron of the arts and letters (and himself a writer and scholar of importance), public benefactor on an imperial scale, not only in Athens but elsewhere in Greece and Asia Minor, holder of many important posts, friend and kinsman of emperors."

[3] Aspasia Annia Regilla
Aspasia Annia Regilla (c. 130 – c. 160 AD), also known as Regilla or Appia Annia Regilla, was a Roman noblewoman who married Herodes Atticus around 140 AD. She was the daughter of Lucius Appius Maximus Norbanus and Aspasia Annia Regilla (her mother). She bore Herodes several children: Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes (who died young), Lucius Vibullius Hipparchus Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes (who became consul in 185 AD), Vibia Aurelia Sabina (who married Marcus Ummidius Quadratus Annianus Verus), Vibia Aurelia Claudia Tisamenis (who married Gaius Julius Severus), Vibia Aurelia Claudia Athenais (who married Marcus Valerius Eudaemon), Vibia Aurelia Claudia Alcibiades (who died young), Vibia Aurelia Claudia Agrippina (who died young), and Vibia Aurelia Claudia Vibullia Alcia Agrippina (who died young). [4] Second Sophistic
The Second Sophistic was a literary movement that flourished during the Roman Empire from approximately 50 AD to 250 AD. It was characterized by a revival of classical Greek rhetoric and style in both prose and poetry. Prominent figures included Dio Chrysostom, Aelius Aristides, Philostratus, and Herodes Atticus himself. The movement emphasized eloquence, imitation of classical models (especially Demosthenes and Plato), and often involved public declamations in Greek cities across the empire.

[5] Lucius Vibullius Hipparchus Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes
Lucius Vibullius Hipparchus Tiberius Claudius Atticus Herodes (born c. 160 AD) was the son of Herodes Atticus and Aspasia Annia Regilla. He followed in his father's footsteps as a prominent figure in Roman society, serving as consul ordinarius in 185 AD. Like his father, he was deeply involved in Greek cultural life and patronage during the period known as the Second Sophistic. He continued his father's legacy as a patron of arts and letters in Athens and other parts of Greece.

[3] Party leaders of the United States House of Representatives
Starting with Republican Nicholas Longworth in 1925, and continued through the Democrats' control of the House from 1931 to 1995, save for Republican majorities in 1947–49 and 1953–55, all majority leaders have directly ascended to the Speakership brought upon by the retirement of the incumbent. The only exceptions during this period were Charles A. Halleck who became Republican House leader and Minority Leader from 1959 to 1965, Hale Boggs who died in a plane crash, and Dick Gephardt who became the Democrats' House leader but as Minority Leader since his party lost control in the 1994 midterm elections. Since 1995, the only Majority Leader to become Speaker is John Boehner, though indirectly as his party lost control in the 2006 midterms elections. He subsequently served as Republican House leader and Minority Leader from 2007 to 2011 and then was elected Speaker when the House reconvened in 2011. In 1998, with Speaker Newt Gingrich announcing his resignation, both Majority Leader Dick Armey and Majority Whip Tom DeLay did not contest the Speakership which eventually went to Chief Deputy Whip Dennis Hastert.

Based on the documents provided, specifically Document [1], the **Republican Party** gained control of the House of Representatives in the 1946 midterm elections, ending 16 years of Democratic control. Joseph William Martin, Jr. became the Speaker of the House.

While Document [1] focuses on the House, historical context (and the phrasing "gained control of congress" implying both chambers) indicates that Republicans also won a majority in the Senate in 1946. The new Congress (the 80th United States Congress) convened and the new leadership took office on **January 3, 1947**. This is when they took control of the "determiner of rules" (the Speaker of the House and the Senate Majority Leader/President pro tempore who set Senate rules).

Document [2] confirms that each House determines its own rules, and Document [3] confirms the Speaker is the presiding officer and leader of the majority party in the House. The transition occurs at the start of the new Congress following the election.

Document [2] explicitly notes that Time Warner Cable acquired systems from the bankrupt Adelphia (some of which were temporarily held by Windjammer Communications before being integrated). Given that Empire Sports Network was a regional network serving this specific upstate New York region, Time Warner Cable is the direct successor to the owner in that market.

Exact Answer: Time Warner Cable
